topic: What if light kept getting slower every hour?

script.text: Hour thirty-four. Deep underground. Light now crawls slower than an ant. The lamps are on, but when you lift your hand, you see it move two seconds later.
Ellie is asleep on a camp bed next to Mom. Mo is snoring. Somewhere above you, the city is freezing in the dark. Down here, it's warm. For now.
You find a bathroom with a mirror. You stand perfectly still. And you wait for your reflection to catch up.
It does. Then it smiles. You didn't smile.
Then your reflection slowly lifts its hand, and points at something behind you.
Light only ever shows you the past. That's the rule. So what is this mirror showing you?
What would you do? Get on the bus, or go back for your mom? Tell me in the comments.

And is any of this real? The science is. Sunlight takes eight minutes to reach us. Without it, Earth freezes in a week. And GPS needs light to keep its speed. And what's in that mirror? You'll find out in part two.
